title: Amazing Animal Feet! Paws, Claws and Toes for Kids
description:
Whose feet are these? Pick your answer with Milo the bluebird, then look closely: a polar bear has wide feet like paddles with tiny bumps that help it grip the ice, a tiger can pull its long claws in and out and can swim across big rivers, and a hippo spreads its four toes wide to walk on the soft river bottom.
An interactive animal lesson for kids ages 2-6, with questions to answer, counting, actions to copy, quick checks and a quiz at the end.
facts: Polar bear: wide, large, paddle-like feet; 5 toes on each foot; claws non-retractable, 5-7 cm long; soles of feet have small dermal bumps (papillae) that may help with traction on ice; even foot pads are furred in winter; covered with fur except for the nose; 5-10 cm of fat, and both fat and pelt provide insulation (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Polar Bear', Physical Characteristics, ielc.libguides.com/sdzg/factsheets/polarbear/characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

Tiger: long, retractable claws on broad forepaws; large curved claws, 80-100 mm (3-4 in) long; dark stripes on body, limbs, head and tail provide camouflage in forests and grasslands (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Tiger', Physical Characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).
Tigers can cross rivers 6-8 km (4-5 mi) wide (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Tiger', Behavior & Ecology, read Nov 16 2026).

Hippo: four functional toes with wide splay; nail-like hooves on the ends of the toes; partial webbing on the feet; being able to splay the digits is a good adaptation for walking in water on soft river bottoms; mucous glands secrete a thick, oily red fluid that dries like lacquer and protects the thin skin against water loss, sunburn and infection (SDZWA Library fact sheet 'Hippopotamus', Physical Characteristics, read Nov 16 2026).

segments.name: hello
lines: Hello, friends! I am Milo the bluebird.
Today we are learning about amazing animal feet!
Paws, claws and toes. How do animals use them?
Three animal friends will show us. Count them with me. One, two, three!
Wiggle your toes. Let's go!

segments.name: polar_bear

lines.t: Who has big, furry feet, for walking on the snow and the ice?
Is it the polar bear? Or is it the pig?

lines: It is the polar bear!
Here is the fun fact. A polar bear has big, wide feet, like paddles!
Each foot has five toes. Let's count. One, two, three, four, five!

lines.t: How does a polar bear walk on slippery ice? Hmm.

lines: The bottoms of its feet have tiny bumps, that help it grip the ice!
Look at those big paws. Grip, grip, grip!
close:polar_bear
And in winter, even the bottoms of its feet are furry!
Furry feet, like cozy slippers! Fuzzy, warm and snug.
A polar bear is covered with thick fur, everywhere except its nose.
Its claws cannot hide away, like a cat's claws. They are always out. Scritch, scratch!
Say it with me. A polar bear has big, furry feet!
close:host
Can you walk like a polar bear? Big, wide steps. Stomp, stomp!
Now grip the ice with your toes. Grip, grip!

lines.t: Quick check! What helps a polar bear grip the ice? Tiny bumps? Or wheels?

lines: Tiny bumps! Grip, grip. Great job!

short.title: How Does a Polar Bear Walk on Ice? Polar Bear Feet

segments.name: tiger

lines.t: Who has big paws, with claws that can hide away?
Is it the tiger? Or is it the cow?

lines: It is the tiger!
Here is the fun fact. A tiger has big, wide front paws.
And long, curved claws. Each one is about as long as a crayon!

lines.t: Where do the tiger's claws go, when it walks? Hmm.

lines: It pulls them in, and hides them away! When it needs them, out they come!
Soft paws, and hidden claws.
close:tiger
And a tiger can swim! Tigers can swim across rivers that are four or five miles wide.
Splash, splash! Paddle, paddle! What a strong swimmer!
Tigers have stripes on their legs, their heads and their tails, too.
A tiger's stripes help it hide, in the forest and in the tall grass. Can you find the stripes?
Say it with me. A tiger can hide its claws!
close:host
Can you show tiger claws? Hide them in. Now out! In, and out!
Now paddle like a swimming tiger. Paddle, paddle, paddle!

lines.t: Quick check! Can a tiger swim? Yes, or no?

lines: Yes! Tigers can swim across big rivers. You remembered!

short.title: Where Do a Tiger's Claws Go? Tiger Facts

segments.name: hippo

lines.t: Who walks along the bottom of the river?
Is it the hippo? Or is it the cow?

lines: It is the hippo!
Here is the fun fact. A hippo has four toes on each foot. Four toes, on four big feet!
Let's count the toes. One, two, three, four!

lines.t: How does a hippo walk on the soft, squishy river bottom? Hmm.

lines: It spreads its toes out wide! Wide toes are great for walking on the soft river bottom.
Spread your fingers wide, like hippo toes!
close:hippo
A hippo's feet have a little bit of webbing, between the toes.
And at the end of each toe is a little hoof, like a big toenail. A hoof, at the end of every toe!
A hippo's skin makes its own special oil. It dries like a shiny coat.
That oil helps protect the hippo's skin from the sun.
Say it with me. A hippo has four wide toes!
close:host
Can you walk like a hippo? Spread your toes, and step, step, step!
Now walk slowly, along the river bottom. Bounce, bounce!

lines.t: Quick check! How many toes does a hippo have on each foot? Four? Or ten?

lines: Four! One, two, three, four. Super thinking!

short.title: How Many Toes Does a Hippo Have? Hippo Facts

segments.name: quiz
lines: Wow! We met three friends with amazing feet. Now it is quiz time!
Get ready. Think hard!
quiz: Who has tiny bumps on its feet, to grip the ice?
Who can pull its claws in, and out?
Who spreads four wide toes on the river bottom?

segments.name: goodbye
lines: You learned so many new things today.
Grip like a polar bear. Paddle like a tiger. And step like a hippo!
How many toes do you have?
Thank you for learning with me. Bye-bye, friends! See you next time!
